description: Enterprise techniques used by MiniFast, ATT&CK software S9052 (v1.0)
name: MiniFast (S9052)

techniques.comment: [MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to execute a process with elevated privileges using `runas`.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has utilized HTTP POST, GET and PUT requests for communications with the C2.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to archive files and directories using ZIP.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has executed commands using `cmd.exe`.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has encoded C2 instructions with Base64.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has collected data from local files and directories on the victim device.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to move data within the victim machine.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has decoded Base64-encoded tasks from the C2.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to upload files over C2 communications.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has listed files and folders within a specified directory.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to delete files and directories.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to download additional files from C2.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has enumerated logical drives on impacted devices.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)

[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has blended into network traffic by mimicking a Chrome browser using the following User-Agent string: `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/146.0.0.0 Safari/537.36`.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has been delivered within a malicious zip file.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)

[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to check running processes and has returned process names and their PIDs. [MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has also checked its relative parent process.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has created scheduled tasks using the name “WindowsSecurityUpdate.”(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has the ability to terminate a process using its PID.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has leveraged valid digital signatures from SSL[.]com to appear legitimate.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has collected the victim's username, hostname and domain information.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
[MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has collected the username on targeted systems.(Citation: CheckPoint_NimbusManticore_May2026)
